summary: The background note-taking pass now calls a member by the name you gave them, not the name they gave themselves, and an allowed room with no label refuses to start rather than risk two unlabelled rooms reading as one.
details: The note-candidates pass builds its own message batch from the raw record and never resolved a sender's identity against the roster the tag path already uses. A member you have mapped a name for (`identity.toml`) was still attributed by their self-set, changeable platform profile name in that pass's prompt, or by nothing at all ('unknown') if they had set none. It now resolves names the same way every other surface does.

`policy.toml` already stopped putting a raw room id on the model's wire for an unlabelled room (2026-09-23) by rendering a placeholder instead — but two unlabelled rooms then rendered as the same room, silently. An allowed room with no label is now a startup error, the same as a second home room in one group.
limitations: Only the note-candidates pass's own batch is fixed here; any other Dreamer pass that assembles its own transcript rather than going through the tag path's assembler would need the same wiring checked separately.
